selection: Use the ordered PARD flaring kit only if it includes a true 4.75 mm / 3/16 in die and makes 45-degree double/inverted flares
exact_spec: Must clamp and flare 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube; double/inverted flare required; practice on scrap before vehicle lines
next_action: Receipt-check the delivered kit before any line fabrication; if no 4.75 mm / 3/16 in die is present buy or borrow a dedicated brake-line flaring tool
reject_if: Only 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 mm dies are supplied; tool makes only single or ISO bubble flares; clamp slips on 4.75 mm tube
notes: This is the gating tool. Do not assume a 4 mm die is acceptable for 4.75 mm brake tube. TM25805 added a second PARD kit candidate titled 3/16 in to 5/8 in; still require physical practice flares before release.

selection: Use the ordered Harden 3-22 mm mini tube cutter if it cuts 4.75 mm tube squarely
exact_spec: Clean square cuts on 4.75 mm / 3/16 in, 6 mm, and 8 mm tube without crushing
next_action: Receipt-check cutter wheel action and test on scrap tube
reject_if: Cutter spirals, crushes, or leaves a severe burr on 4.75 mm tube
notes: A square cut is mandatory for repeatable double/inverted flares.

selection: Use the ordered internal/external tube deburrer or reamer only if receipt check proves it fits 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube
exact_spec: Must deburr inside and outside of 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube after every cut
next_action: Receipt-check the ordered deburrer/reamer: packaging, tool tip/size, and clean inside/outside deburr on scrap 4.75 mm tube. If missing or too large, buy one compact dedicated small-tube tool.
reject_if: No internal deburrer; only a file or knife is available; burrs remain inside tube
notes: Burrs can crack or distort the flare and can contaminate hydraulics. | Pending audit 2026-05-27: ToolsMart PARD product page and TM25550 order evidence list the flaring/cutting set size/variants, but do not prove a separate deburrer/reamer is included. | User update 2026-05-27 marks this as gettable locally. | User update 2026-05-27: suitable office-runner task only as a labelled tool purchase; Aamir is not responsible for brake-line fabrication judgement. | User update 2026-05-30 says the deburring tool is already ordered; keep fabrication blocked until physical receipt proves a usable internal/external deburr on 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube.

selection: Do not buy a duplicate bender now; use the received Daraz 1/4-5/16-3/8 in bender for larger tube and test/borrow/shop-form any tight 4.75 mm brake-line bends if needed
exact_spec: 4.75 mm / 3/16 in bends must be clean with no flattening or kinking; existing Daraz bender covers 1/4, 5/16, 3/8 only
next_action: No active purchase; test on scrap selected tube before line fabrication and reopen only if practice bends fail
reject_if: Tube wrinkles, flats, kinks, or shop cannot bend required 4.75 mm sections
notes: Received Daraz bender is marked off; exact 4.75 mm bender is a conditional reopen item, not an active still-required purchase.

selection: Buy metric flare-nut/line wrenches before loosening old hydraulic fittings
exact_spec: At minimum cover likely brake-line nut hex sizes around 10, 11, 12, 14, and 17 mm; sample-match on vehicle
next_action: Buy a small set or individual 10x12 plus 12x14 and 14x17 sizes before removal
reject_if: Only open-end spanners are available; wrench flexes or rounds old nuts
notes: Use penetrating oil and the correct line wrench before forcing old fittings.

selection: Use calipers and a metric thread pitch gauge to identify flare nuts and port threads
exact_spec: Must distinguish M10x1.0, M10x1.25, M12x1.0, and any non-metric fitted hardware before buying fittings
next_action: Confirm on hand before fitting purchase
reject_if: Threads are guessed from vehicle year or by eye only
notes: Do not buy flare nuts by catalog logic alone because the brake system has prior conversion history.

selection: Prefer new brake-rated CuNi/Cunifer 4.75 mm / 3/16 in tube; fallback is brake-rated bundy steel
exact_spec: 10000 mm minimum if combining brake and clutch; 12000 mm preferred; no bare copper
next_action: Verify Amir-procured coil label/photo before release: brake-rated 4.75 mm / 3/16 in coated steel tube, 25 ft minimum, no bare copper/plumbing/compression tube; then prove flares on scrap before vehicle fabrication.
reject_if: Bare copper, plumbing tube, used tube, unknown rating, or stainless tube that the shop/tool cannot flare cleanly
notes: CuNi/Cunifer is preferred for in-house shaping because it is easier to bend and flare; bundy steel is acceptable if the fabricator can form clean bends and flares. | User requested zinc-coated/galvanised steel brake tube via Amir on 2026-05-27; reject bare copper, plumbing tube, compression fittings, or unlabelled/unknown tube. | User clarification 2026-05-28: 25 ft zinc-coated/galvanised 3/16 in brake tube is procured by Amir; receipt/spec check still gates use.

selection: Buy new double/inverted flare nuts only after old nut thread and port seat are confirmed
exact_spec: Brake-rated fittings for 4.75 mm / 3/16 in tube; likely Toyota-style metric hardware but sample controls final thread
next_action: Remove one old line intact; photograph straight-on flare face; measure nut thread and seat; then buy extras for practice and final lines
reject_if: Seller offers single flare, ISO bubble, plumbing compression fittings, or cannot match thread/seat
notes: Buy enough extra nuts to allow scrap/practice flares before final lines.

item: Rear axle tee and inline unions
selection: Use on-hand brake tees/unions only where the original item is seized corroded damaged or mismatched
exact_spec: Match thread, flare seat, port orientation, mounting hole/bracket style, tube entry angles, and original location
next_action: Photograph original tee/union locations and compare old fittings to on-hand stock before install
reject_if: Plumbing brass, compression unions, unknown seat, wrong port orientation, or moving line routes to suit a stocked tee
notes: The project has brake tees/unions on hand. Replace at the same locations as before only when the old piece cannot safely be reused; stop and sample-match if no on-hand tee fits.

selection: Define a written hose spec or use mechanic-labelled old samples then buy complete crimped brake flex hose assemblies only if the shop can match the spec exactly
exact_spec: Front left, front right, and rear center; DOT/SAE J1401 or OEM-equivalent; match free length, bracket groove, end fittings/thread/seat/banjo as applicable, hose rating, and fitted route clearance
next_action: Aamir may collect quote/photos immediately. He may pay only against the written spec sheet, a mechanic-labelled old sample, or explicit mechanic/user approval; otherwise call first.
reject_if: Generic roll hose, reused hose, unmatched ends, no brake hydraulic rating, substitute fitting, unknown thread/seat, or any seller judgement that changes the written spec
notes: Do not fabricate flex hoses locally unless the shop is a certified hydraulic brake hose assembler and can match the old fittings. | User correction 2026-05-27: specs can be defined by the project/mechanic; Aamir remains a runner and does not make fitment or brake-safety decisions. | Spec capture guide 2026-05-28 defines the required installed photos, labelled samples, measurements, and release rule before Aamir pays.

selection: Use on-hand rubber-lined P-clips, brake hose U-clips, axle line supports, grommets, edge trim, and plated fasteners by original location
exact_spec: 4.75 mm P-clips plus mixed support hardware matched to measured line OD and old bracket holes; preserve original line routes
next_action: Map original support and hose-clip positions first; replace corroded/missing supports in those same positions with on-hand stock
reject_if: Cable ties, bare metal clips, loose U-clips, unsupported spans, or new support positions that force a different line route
notes: The project has P-clips and U-clips on hand. This is now an install-fit/location-match task, not a shopping task; add new supports only where the original route would otherwise rub or span unsafely.

selection: Use on-hand/workshop caps/plugs, brake cleaner, catch bottle or bleeder kit, rags, and catch tray before opening lines
exact_spec: DOT 3 fluid, clear bleed hose, and nitrile gloves are already received; remaining setup is managed from on-hand/workshop supplies and must be physically ready before disassembly
next_action: Verify the on-hand/workshop setup before the first hydraulic fitting is opened
reject_if: No line caps/plugs; no catch bottle/tray; brake cleaner unavailable
notes: Open ports should still be capped immediately; this row is a workstream safety gate, not a purchase task.

selection: Reserve extra tube length and spare flare nuts for bench practice
exact_spec: Make at least 5 practice double/inverted flares on the selected tube before fabricating vehicle lines
next_action: Practice cut/deburr/flare sequence and inspect flare symmetry before cutting final lines
reject_if: First flare attempted on final vehicle line; flare is off-center, cracked, folded unevenly, or nut was forgotten
notes: Practice confirms tool setup, die depth, deburring, and nut orientation.
